subject.title: BL-ecommerce-coupons-28: stripe bypass uses exact equality without rounding tolerance

question: Should ecommerce coupon validation waive Stripe payment when the rounded residual is at most €0.01, or should residual cents continue through payment handling?
rationale: The code change is narrow, but deciding to treat a one-cent residual as free is a business and checkout policy choice rather than a purely mechanical refactor.

options.title: Accept one-cent tolerance
options.body: Land the linked PR path if the ecommerce owner accepts waiving at most €0.01 to avoid Stripe charges for effectively free coupon orders.

options.title: Keep strict payment handling
options.body: Close or revise the linked PR if every positive residual must still be charged or handled by Stripe/payment code.

options.title: Choose a different threshold
options.body: Revise the PR to encode a different residual rule and add focused validation evidence for the selected boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept one-cent tolerance
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR path if the ecommerce owner accepts waiving at most €0.01 to avoid Stripe charges for effectively free coupon orders.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue and related BL mother issue identify MiguelHamelyn as the coupons business-rule owner for this policy choice.
